messages:
Maya: Quick sync — I'm proposing we deprecate the service-bridge shim over the next 3 quarters. It's accumulating tech debt and blocks clean routing for Dedicated/Private modes.
Chris: +1. Can you outline the migration plan? worried about customer-facing config changes.
Maya: Plan sketch: 1) Introduce contract-normalizer sidecar in runtime for 2 sprints. 2) Gradually flip producers to publish normalized contracts. 3) Remove bridge after 75% traffic qualifies. Timeline: Q2 spike + Q3 rollout + Q4 decomm.
Sam: How do we handle older Dedicated deployments where customers pin versions?
Maya: Two levers: a) keep bridge in a compatibility release train for Dedicated eligible customers (opt-in) b) provide a compatibility shim package for on-prem installs with an extended support window.
Leo: What about observability? We'll need signal parity before flipping. Token-level tracing and route tags must be present.
Anna: Agree. Also need a safety net: auto-fallback to bridge if normalized contract validation fails. That reduces blast radius.
Chris: Can we avoid a global flag flip? Prefer per-tenant rollout with canary percent and feature-gated routing.
Maya: Yes — per-tenant rollout. We'll add the rollout policy in the router: "contract_version_policy": {"mode":"per-tenant","canary_pct":10}.
Sam: Ops runbook request: how to detect a bad normalization? Suggested checks: 1) 5xx rate delta 2) mismatched output schema rate 3) latency p95 regressions.
Anna: I'll add a regression alert: eval-prompt-set mismatches + auto-rollback if mismatch > 1% over 10m.
Leo: Work items for infra: - add sidecar image build + canary helm/ship chart - expose rollout API - tracing tags. ETA 3 weeks for spike.
Maya: Owner assignments: Anna (validation & alerts), Leo (infra & rollout API), Chris (customer comms & Dedicated compatibility), Sam (on-prem shim docs). I'll draft RFC with migration checklist tomorrow.
Chris: Can we include a small compatibility CLI to translate legacy to normalized contracts for customers doing offline migration?
Anna: Good idea. We can ship a node/python translator and a k8s Job template. Keep it backward-compatible with bridge->normalized mapping rules.
infra-bot: Deploy check: infra pipeline will need a new e2e job to run normalization sanity on each canary deploy.
Maya: Risk & rollback: worst-case we re-enable bridge per-tenant and roll forward fixes. Low-risk because bridge stays available during the roll.
Sam: Customers with strict audit: we'll provide a policy doc and a support window of 9 months.
Maya: OK — next steps: I'll open RFC PR tonight with timeline, owners, and a short checklist. Ping me in #eng-runtime if you want to be on the spike. :thumbsup:
Chris: Thanks — please flag any customer-facing blockers in the PR so we can coordinate comms.
Anna: I'll prototype validation alerts during the spike and attach the alert playbook to the RFC.
Maya: Great. Closing for now — will post RFC link here.
